window.note: PROVEME — the rule got ONE spelling and TWO seats, and the corpus went to zero. cairn/tools/base/address_rule.py is now the single definition of a hand-spelled instance address, as an AST predicate over an EXPRESSION rather than a text scan: a mention lives in an ast.Constant and a spelling is an ast.BinOp, which is why the old watcher's exclude-my-own-file-by-name is gone rather than re-implemented. SEAT ONE, build time: build_inspector's address_is_resolved_never_spelled sieve, registered 21st, attributing by deepest owner (address.component_of) so a holder never wears its nested machine's finding. SEAT TWO, pulse time: cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/does_the_address_gate_bite.py, which reads the REGISTRY as well as the count, because zero sites is what a working gate and a deleted one both produce. MEASURED: 0 hand-spelled sites over 274 files, two exemptions each bearing weight at exactly one line (cairn/tools/base/address.py:94 and cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_fence.py:285) — the cast predicted THREE exemptions and the AST shape retired the third. PROOFS GREEN TWICE UNDER NETNS: build_inspector 3/3 (incl. the new test_address_sieve.py, defect-first with nine teeth because the corpus was converted in the same voyage and the sieve was born green), inference_domain 5/5 (incl. the new tooth that the overlay berths at the resolved instance address), aider_shim 7/7, ground_loop 5/5, tools/base 19/20 — the one red being the pre-existing filed trouble test_watchme_spec.py, which this voyage did not touch. TWO DEFECTS CAUGHT MID-BUILD BY STANDING PHYSICS, both fixed. (1) hand_spelled_instance_paths._enough had the signature (now, context) while Probe.gathered_enough calls enough(context) — it had never raised because nothing pulses base's shim; censused across all 30 probes carrying an enough, n=1, and it was the file this ticket owns. (2) test_probe_carry's corpus tooth redded the new probe on arrival for carrying its ticket as a bare id instead of a path built by owning_ticket() — the 2026-08-05 ruling made physics, doing exactly its job. AND THE LOOP CAUGHT ME TOO: the beat at 00:46:55Z benched the base device on a real ImportError from a window in this build (walk_py not yet exported from cairn.tools.import_sieve). Fixed on disk, and the bench then survived a clear because the two-day-old daemon held the pre-export module; restarted (pid 973171), verified through the loop's own discover(), cleared through TroubleDevice.clear, and base is back on the roster at 20 subscribers.

window.note: WATCHME(the_address_gate_bites) — armed at cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/does_the_address_gate_bite.py, which is the berth the ticket's spec names, and THIS CROSSING IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT IT IS ARMED: the emission gate resolves the spec's probe path and raises WatchmeEmissionRed on an unarmed one, so a passing crossing is the instrument, not a claim about it. THE PROBE BERTHS WITH WHAT IT WATCHES, NOT WITH THE TICKET IT WAS COMPILED FROM — the thing being watched is the SIEVE REGISTRY, which is build_inspector's, so the probe sits there even though the ticket's component is cairn/tools/base. The corpus half of the same question is read without authority by the resolver's own watch at cairn/tools/base/probes/hand_spelled_instance_paths.py; this one reads BOTH halves. WHY BOTH, and it is the whole design: a count alone cannot tell a working gate from a deleted one — a rule dropped out of build_inspector.SIEVES leaves the corpus reading clean, and 0 sites is what a live gate and an absent gate both print. So the carry names three states that a bare zero collapses: gate_absent (the sieve is not registered), gate_did_not_bite (a site stands while the sieve IS registered — the gate is present and green anyway), and vacuous (files_read == 0, a scan that read nothing, indistinguishable from a clean corpus at the moment the instrument broke). ENOUGH IS DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC, per the ticket: ONE hand-spelled site standing in a component built after this ticket lands is STRONG falsification and satisfies alone, because a green gate gets leaned on and that is worse than no gate; THREE consecutive non-vacuous readings at zero, at least one taken after a component that NEEDED instance state was built, is WEAK confirmation and also satisfies. A vacuous reading counts toward neither and is itself a red. READ AT ARMING (n=0 toward the horizon, and recorded so a later reading has a baseline that is not a memory): 0 hand-spelled sites over 276 files, sieve registered, 3 exemptions each bearing weight at exactly one line, would_trigger False, enough False, readings_needed_to_confirm 3, readings_seen 0. The at_proved snapshot the probe carries reads 0 sites over 274 files with 3 exemptions — so the corpus has grown by two files since the PROVED-side measurement and stayed at zero, which is the only kind of clean reading that means anything here.
